statusText: Calm but slightly more mixed conditions extend into the deep European morning; NQ futures inch lower and S&P/Dow futures sit flat-to-marginally-higher with no confirmed gap or failed-pullback structure, while Asia's session cools from the prior run's outsized gains into a dispersed picture (Nikkei +0.44%, Kospi +1.14%, but Hang Seng -0.93%, CSI 300 -0.12%, ASX 200 -0.92%) and VIX holds near a fresh recent low (~14.5-14.7). Alpha Vantage remains fully rate-limited for a fourth consecutive run (daily quota exhausted), so this assessment again relies entirely on WebSearch.
recommendation: Current action remains EA_ON. headline: Nasdaq-100 futures inch lower and S&P/Dow futures hold near flat into the deep European morning as Asia's rally cools into a more mixed session (Nikkei +0.44%, Kospi +1.14%, but Hang Seng -0.93%, CSI 300 -0.12%, ASX 200 -0.92%) -- VIX holds near a fresh recent low (~14.5-14.7), 10Y ~4.65% -- with today's Retail Sales (12:30 UTC) and cash open still the session's main checkpoints; Alpha Vantage remains fully rate-limited for a fourth consecutive run, so this assessment again relies entirely on WebSearch.
body: About three minutes past the top of the hour and roughly one hour past the prior run, and about 8.5 hours after Thursday's 20:00 UTC cash close, conditions remain broadly calm into the deep European morning, though the cross-asset picture has turned somewhat more mixed than the prior run. Bloomberg's overnight wrap reports Nasdaq-100 futures 'inched lower' while S&P 500 futures traded near the flatline and Dow futures added just 37 points -- a quiet, low-amplitude handover with no confirmed gap or failed-pullback structure, continuing off Thursday's record closes (S&P 500 7,798.99, Nasdaq Composite 26,803.03, Dow 53,839.99). Asia's session has cooled from the prior run's outsized gains into a more dispersed picture: Japan's Nikkei 225 +0.44% and Topix +0.49%, South Korea's Kospi +1.14% (Kosdaq -0.57%), but Hong Kong's Hang Seng -0.93%, mainland China's CSI 300 -0.12% and Australia's ASX 200 -0.92% -- MSCI Asia Pacific still +0.3% on the day (+2.6% on the week) but the breadth is now conflicting rather than uniformly firmer, consistent with profit-taking after Wednesday-Thursday's rally rather than a fresh directional catalyst. This keeps Applied Materials' tepid post-earnings reaction read as company-specific: no evidence of broader semiconductor-equipment transmission has emerged across multiple runs. VIX holds near a fresh recent low, last quoted 14.53-14.70 (little changed from the prior run's ~14.5), and the 10-year Treasury yield remains around 4.65%, essentially unchanged; oil settled Thursday down over 2% (WTI $81.25, Brent $87.07) with no new overnight data point found. Geopolitically, the Strait of Hormuz standoff continues unresolved -- Iran's IRGC reiterated Thursday that no vessel may transit without its permission, and Iran's parliament continues reviewing a bill to bar US/Israel-linked vessels pending war-damage compensation -- but no new kinetic escalation has been identified since the prior run; the Ukraine-Russia war likewise shows no fresh market-moving escalation. Alpha Vantage's free-tier daily quota remains exhausted for a fourth consecutive run -- the TREASURY_YIELD call was retried once and returned an immediate rate_limit error both times -- so, per the fallback protocol, this assessment again relies entirely on WebSearch for yields, oil, VIX, equities and price-path context; Confidence stays in the medium-low band, reflecting that reduced evidence base, the continued absence of a directly-confirmed live NQ/QQQ intraday chart, and some cross-source timing inconsistency in the Asia figures (today's in-session moves vs. yesterday's closing prints), partially offset by solid corroboration on VIX, yields, oil and Hormuz status this run. Tail holds low at 9% (calm, no persistent one-way structure; the futures move is negligible and Asia's dispersion argues against directional efficiency) while Stress ticks up to 27% (from 23% last run) to reflect the newly conflicting cross-asset breadth, with the approaching Retail Sales, cash open and preliminary UMich sentiment cluster still the main driver of the forecast Stress path higher into early afternoon UTC before easing back through the evening and into the next Asia handover.
